findings.title: Exposed MySQL Service
findings.description: The MySQL database service is publicly accessible, increasing the attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Restrict MySQL access to internal networks or specific trusted IPs only.

findings.title: Exposed Backup File
findings.description: A backup of a configuration file was found, potentially containing sensitive information.
findings.recommendation: Remove all publicly accessible backup or temporary files from the web server.

findings.title: Open Uploads Directory
findings.description: The /uploads directory is publicly browsable, which could allow for arbitrary file uploads.
findings.recommendation: Disable directory listing for /uploads and implement strict file type and size validation.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options headers are missing, increasing risk of clickjacking and MIME type sniffing attacks.
findings.recommendation: Implement X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options headers with appropriate security policies.

findings.title: Outdated Nginx Version
findings.description: Nginx version 1.20.1 is outdated and may contain known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Update Nginx to the latest stable version to mitigate known security flaws.

findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: The 'id' GET parameter is vulnerable to boolean-based blind SQL injection, allowing for unauthorized database access.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Nginx Chunked Encoding Bypass
findings.description: An Nginx chunked encoding vulnerability allows for remote code execution on the web server.
findings.recommendation: Apply the latest security patches for Nginx to address the chunked encoding vulnerability.

findings.title: Weak TLS Protocol Support
findings.description: The server supports insecure TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 protocols, making it vulnerable to downgrade attacks.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, enforcing a minimum of TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3.

findings.title: Weak Cipher Suites Enabled
findings.description: The server supports weak RC4 cipher suites, which are known to be cryptographically insecure.
findings.recommendation: Disable all weak cipher suites, especially those using RC4, and prioritize strong, modern ciphers.

findings.title: Exposed Development Subdomain
findings.description: A 'dev' subdomain was discovered, potentially hosting unpatched code or sensitive information.
findings.recommendation: Secure or remove development environments that are publicly accessible.

findings.title: API Subdomain Discovered
findings.description: An API subdomain was found, indicating a potential attack surface for API-specific vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Thoroughly audit the API endpoints for common API security vulnerabilities like BOLA and IDOR.

findings.title: CORS Wildcard Origin
findings.description: The server allows requests from any origin via a wildcard in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.
findings.recommendation: Restrict CORS to specific, trusted origins instead of using a wildcard.

findings.title: Publicly Readable S3 Bucket
findings.description: An AWS S3 bucket named 'ttvideodownload-assets' is publicly readable, exposing sensitive files.
findings.recommendation: Configure S3 bucket policies to block public access and restrict permissions to authorized entities.

findings.title: Exposed Kubernetes Dashboard
findings.description: The Kubernetes dashboard is exposed publicly and allows unauthenticated access to sensitive API endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Implement strong authentication and authorization for the Kubernetes dashboard or remove public exposure.

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
findings.description: An IDOR vulnerability allows unauthorized users to access other users' video data by manipulating the video ID.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust authorization checks at every API endpoint to ensure users can only access their own resources.

findings.title: AWS Access Key Leak
findings.description: An AWS Access Key ID was found publicly exposed in an environment configuration file.
findings.recommendation: Immediately revoke the compromised AWS key and ensure sensitive credentials are not stored in publicly accessible files.

findings.title: Database Password in Config File
findings.description: A database password was found hardcoded in a configuration file, posing a significant security risk.
findings.recommendation: Store database credentials securely using environment variables or a secrets management service.

findings.title: Cloudflare WAF Detected
findings.description: Cloudflare Web Application Firewall is detected, providing a layer of protection against common web attacks.
findings.recommendation: Understand WAF rules and consider advanced WAF features to enhance protection.

findings.title: SMB Null Session Allowed
findings.description: An SMB null session is permitted on a critical internal server, allowing unauthenticated enumeration of shares.
findings.recommendation: Disable null sessions on SMB servers to prevent unauthorized access to share information.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover Vulnerability
findings.description: The subdomain 'blog.ttvideodownload.me' points to an unclaimed SaaS service, enabling subdomain takeover.
findings.recommendation: Reclaim the dangling DNS record or update the CNAME to point to a valid, controlled resource.

agents.command: msfconsole -q -x "use auxiliary/scanner/http/http_login..." && hydra -L users.txt ttvideodownload.me http-post-form
amass enum -passive -d ttvideodownload.me && theHarvester -d ttvideodownload.me -b all
python3 cors_scanner.py -u https://ttvideodownload.me && python3 ssrf_scanner.py -u https://ttvideodownload.me
kr scan https://ttvideodownload.me -w routes-large.kite && restler --target https://ttvideodownload.me
cme smb ttvideodownload.me -u '' -p '' && bloodhound-python -d ttvideodownload.me -u null -p null -c All
subzy run --targets subdomains.txt && nuclei -tags takeover -u https://ttvideodownload.me
